Contributing

The safe-change workflow, style rules, and where to add games, lessons, skills and explainers.

Use when: You want to add a game, lesson, skill or fix — safely.

Ground rules #

  • License: MIT. Keep headers and the LICENSE file intact.
  • Zero dependencies: PRs that add runtime packages need a superseding ADR (see Security & privacy).
  • Docs-with-code: any behaviour change updates the relevant canonical .md guide in the same PR, then runs npm run docs:build. npm run docs:check is the merge gate.

The safe-change workflow #

  1. Fork and clone; open index.html or run a local server.
  2. Make the change in the owning module (Architecture tells you which).
  3. Run the quality gates — at minimum npm run check and a visual pass over affected views in desktop + mobile widths.
  4. Update docs + changelog (docs/.docs/changelog.md).
  5. Open a PR describing what changed, evidence of gates run, and screenshots for UI changes.

Where things get added #

You want to add…Touch
A new skill/topicjs/data.js skill graph (id, grade band, lens tags, dims)
A lessonjs/data.js lessons + the Learn view renders it automatically
A gamejs/data.js game registry + a renderer in js/app.js Play section
A question generatorjs/engine.js generators + wire its id into quiz intents
A chat explainer or solverjs/app.js chat brain — see Mathaloid Brain
Visual stylingcss/atlas.css using existing tokens — see Design system

Style rules #

  • Vanilla JS (ES2020), template-literal rendering, no frameworks.
  • Escape all user-echoed text with esc().
  • Keep functions small and colocated with their view; prefer data-driven content in data.js over hardcoded HTML.
  • Every interactive element needs keyboard focus and a visible focus style.
